Concrete · Pavers · Turf in Avalon Park, FL

Concrete, Pavers and Artificial Turf for Avalon Park Homes

Opera pours concrete and lays pavers and artificial turf for Avalon Park, a 1,860-acre unincorporated Orange County community east of Orlando built around a Town Center and roughly 250 acres of man-made lakes. A concrete driveway here falls in the $6–$15 per sq ft installed market range this October, reviewed through Orange County's own permit process rather than a city hall.

By the Opera Concrete & Pavers estimating team · Updated October 1, 2026

No city hall here: Orange County runs every permit

Avalon Park was never incorporated as its own town; it's an unincorporated Orange County community, so every driveway, slab or paver job inside it is reviewed by the county's own Division of Building Safety rather than a city office (Orange County, Do I Need a Permit). The county's own language is blunt about it: "anytime you are pouring concrete or placing pavers, a permit is required," with pavers specifically routed through a zoning permit rather than the fuller building-permit review a poured slab gets (Orange County, Residential Pavers).

A 1998 planned development built as its own village cluster

Orange County approved Avalon Park as a 1,860-acre Planned Development in 1998, a Traditional Neighborhood Development laid out in New Urbanism fashion around a central Town Center, with roughly 3,400 single-family homes and 1,431 multifamily units built out around it (Orange County Government, Avalon Park; Avalon Park Orlando, About). That PD status means a homeowner here answers to both the county's standard permit review and the project's own county-approved design standards, a second layer most unincorporated Orange County lots don't carry.

Two hundred fifty acres of lakes built into the site plan

Avalon Park's own description of itself counts 240 acres of preserved wetlands, 400 acres of upland preserve and 250 acres of man-made lakes woven through its villages (Avalon Park Orlando, About), acreage that exists because the ground under much of east Orange County drains poorly to begin with. Myakka and Smyrna, the two flatwoods soil series most common across this stretch of the county, are both built on a shallow, slow-moving water table that the USDA pegs within a foot and a half of grade for part of a typical year (NRCS soil survey, Smyrna series), a drainage profile the development's own lake network was clearly sized around rather than fought.

The county's own driveway spec, inches and feet

Orange County's residential lot-grading policy spells out the driveway apron itself: a minimum 6-inch-thick, 3,000-psi slab, set back at least 3 feet from the property line, with one driveway allowed per lot where the frontage runs under 100 feet (Orange County, Residential Lot Grading Policy). A retaining wall holding back more than 4 feet of fill, or one over 2 feet that also resists a lateral load, needs its own signed and sealed engineering under the county's residential plan guide (Orange County, A Guide for Residential Plan Approval).

Newer construction than most of the Orange County towns nearby

Avalon Park's villages have been filling in since the PD's 1998 approval, which puts the bulk of its driveways, patios and pool decks at under three decades old, younger than the median home in Winter Park, Belle Isle or Maitland. Younger concrete here means resurfacing is the exception rather than the rule, and most calls into the community are for new work rather than replacing an original 1980s pour.

Frequently asked questions

Does Avalon Park have its own building department?

No. Avalon Park is unincorporated Orange County, so the county's Division of Building Safety reviews every driveway, slab and paver permit rather than a city office (Orange County, Do I Need a Permit).

Is a paver patio reviewed differently than a poured concrete one in Avalon Park?

Yes, under county rules. Pouring concrete needs a building permit, while placing pavers on a driveway or walkway goes through a zoning permit instead, a lighter review with its own fee and site-plan requirement.

Why does Avalon Park have so many ponds and lakes built into it?

The 1998 planned development set aside 250 acres for man-made lakes alongside 240 acres of wetlands and 400 acres of upland preserve, acreage that also answers to the poorly drained flatwoods soil underneath much of the surrounding area.

Does Avalon Park's HOA add anything on top of the county permit?

The community sits inside a county-approved Planned Development with its own design standards, on top of the standard permit review, so an exterior project here typically clears both the county's sign-off and the development's own architectural process.

Is Avalon Park's concrete newer than other Orange County communities?

Generally yes. The development has been building out since 1998, so most of its driveways, patios and pool decks are still under three decades old, younger than the typical home in several incorporated Orange County cities nearby.

What should a homeowner in Avalon Park confirm before hiring a contractor?

Nail down whether the job needs the county's full building permit or the lighter zoning permit that covers pavers, ask how the quote accounts for the development's own design review on top of that, and run the company through the state's license search before signing.
